stem: Air temperature and RH are stable, but measured leaf temperature drops several degrees after airflow increases. What should change in plant-level VPD interpretation?
choices: Use the changed leaf temperature because leaf-to-air vapor-pressure interpretation can differ from air-only VPD
Keep the same plant-level VPD because stable room air temperature and RH are sufficient to represent the crop boundary layer
Attribute the lower leaf temperature mainly to instrument variation unless room air temperature also changes
Use fertilizer EC as the primary correction factor because nutrient concentration strongly determines the leaf-to-air vapor-pressure gradient
rationale: Leaf temperature can differ from air temperature as radiation, airflow, and transpiration change. Plant-level vapor-pressure interpretation should account for that measured leaf temperature.
